title: A jackal quotes the earth as family
hook: a jackal wins a deer's friendship with a famous verse; the verse is true, and the fable knows who to watch
carry: vasudhaiva kutumbakam: to a wide heart, earth is family
tomorrow: once the joins come apart, which words are left?

segments.voice: Yesterday, atithidevo bhava: welcome the guest as god, the one who turns up with no fixed date. Today the circle gets much wider, and a jackal does the quoting.
screen: `LET THE GUEST BE A GOD TO YOU.`

segments.voice: The Hitopadesha is a book of fables made for teaching young princes. In one, a deer lives in a forest with an old friend, a crow. One day a jackal strolls up to the deer, all charm. Let's be friends, he says. The crow is wary: you don't even know where he's from. And the jackal answers with a verse. This one is mine, that one is a stranger: that's how small minds count. To the generous of heart, the whole earth is family. Vasudhaiva kutumbakam.
screen: `A DEER, A CROW, A JACKAL.` → `THIS ONE'S MINE, THAT ONE'S A STRANGER?` → `VASUDHAIVA KUTUMBAKAM.`

segments.voice: The deer is won over. And, without spoiling it, the crow turns out to be the friend worth having. Hindus quote that verse as one of their best lines, and it stands in the Maha Upanishad too, as a teaching. The fable's joke is that even the best line can be borrowed by a jackal. It doesn't make the line less true. So why should the earth be family? Hindu thought gives a reason this week has already met: the same Self lives in every being. The Isha Upanishad says it plainly. Whoever sees all beings in the Self, and the Self in all beings, turns away from no one. If tat tvam asi is true of you, it's true of the stranger. That's the root of the wide heart. Even the sound folds together: vasudha, the earth, and eva, indeed, meet as vasudhaiva. A neighbor tradition says something close. In the New Testament, Paul, speaking to strangers in Athens, says God hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth. Those are the King James words, Acts 17. Both lines reach past one's own people. The honest difference is where they start. Paul starts from one Creator and one shared origin. The Upanishads start from one Self, seen by a wide heart.
screen: `EVEN A JACKAL CAN QUOTE IT.` · `ONE SELF IN EVERY BEING.` · `ACTS 17: OF ONE BLOOD.` · `ONE CREATOR; ONE SELF.` · then, large: `THE EARTH IS ONE FAMILY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone outside your circle: a new kid, a neighbor you've never spoken to, someone whose faith isn't yours. Picture their face, and say quietly, in the Upanishads' way: the same Self lives in them. If you pray, add their name to your prayer tonight. If you don't, wish them one good thing. Then rest the hands, and stay with the breath.
Sandhi plainly: the meeting of words. Today, a and e becoming ai, and the earth as one family folded into vasudhaiva.
For the road: vasudhaiva kutumbakam, to a wide heart, the earth is family. That's the last join this week.

howItsDone: Hindus quote vasudhaiva kutumbakam as a call to treat the whole earth as family; Sanskrit students learn the a + e = ai join by splitting it into vasudha and eva.

fork.setup: at a school assembly someone says, 'every faith teaches exactly the same thing: we're one family.' a friend asks if that's right. what do you say?
options: some lines share it, like Acts 17 and the Maha Upanishad, but they start from different places.
yes: every tradition says it in the very same way.
no: only one tradition really teaches it.
fork.reveal: shared, and honestly different: Paul starts from one Creator and one blood; the Upanishads from one Self in every being, seen by a wide heart. neither is ranked.

original.note: Sanskrit: the earth, indeed, is a family (Maha Upanishad).

trapdoor: what you thought: a modern slogan about world peace.
what it means: vasudha eva kutumbakam, the earth indeed is a family, for the generous of heart, because one Self lives in every being.
what a scholar hears: a + e gives ai (vriddhi, Ashtadhyayi 6.1.88); the Maha Upanishad verse sets it against counting 'mine' and 'a stranger's.'
